scope: Complete exact source and six expanded declaration types/axiom reports for the original real-coordinate finite descent consumer. Reuses sealed inverse substitution, finite physical descent and coefficient-growth reviews; no broad foundation audit.
evidence_category: Lean kernel-compiled finite polynomial evaluation, homogeneous degrees and geometric coefficient-L1 estimates, conditional on balance of the actual spinor-substituted support.

findings.reason: The input P is a genuine complex-coefficient polynomial in the four original real KS coordinates. A(P) and B(P) are exactly the previously defined finite descent polynomials applied to ksRealPolynomialToSpinor P. The left side of the physical identity evaluates P at the original Complex.ofReal(y_i), not at an unrelated transformed input.

The inverse substitution physical evaluation theorem rewrites the original-coordinate input into its actual spinor/conjugate evaluation. The sealed finite physical descent theorem then gives A(ksMap y)+norm(y)^2*B(ksMap y) for every y, including zero. No domain exclusion, inverse radius or root choice is introduced.

Every theorem requiring balance states it on the actual support of ksRealPolynomialToSpinor P, with d0+d1=d2+d3. It is not incorrectly imposed on the original-coordinate support, and it is not yet derived from physical circle invariance.

Original homogeneity 2m is preserved by the linear inverse substitution. The existing finite descent theorem therefore yields A homogeneous of degree m and B homogeneous of degree m-1, with a separate B=0 clause at m=0. Zero outputs remain allowed.

The proof applies polynomialCoeffL1_balanced_radial_degree_bound to the substituted polynomial and then uses whole-L1 contraction to bound the result by L1(P)*2^m. It does not apply a coefficientwise geometric theorem to the substituted polynomial using an unproved preservation premise.

The explicit coefficient hypothesis ||P.coeff d||<=M*B^(2m) concerns original P and its original support. The homogeneous counting bound gives L1(P)<=M*(4B)^(2m). Multiplication by 2^m yields exactly M*(32*B^2)^m. The endpoint contains no additional hidden norm or coefficient assumptions.

Only M>=0 and B>=0 are assumed; no inverse of either appears. At m=0 the geometric right side is M, and the odd output vanishes. M=0 or B=0 with m>0 forces all supported input coefficients to vanish under the explicit premise, consistent with the zero output bound.

All conclusions concern the literal finite MvPolynomial transformations and actual coefficient sums. No analytic Taylor identification, infinite summation, balanced-support derivation or executable arithmetic claim is hidden in the statements.
